# SFX style and density

**Which sound effects, and how many?** · [all approaches](index.md) · clashes: C13


## A sound on every visual event
<a id="every-event"></a>

Whoosh for movement, pop for text, chime for success, thud or click for impact; UI clicks on screen recordings.

**Looks like:** Every label pops, every slide whooshes, every tick chimes, the final rep thuds. Without it the edit feels like a 'silent movie'.

**Good at:** retention; polish; makes graphics feel physical

**Weak at:** can turn into clutter; time to place

**Best for:** formats reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches all · goals retention · effort medium

**How:** Edits/CapCut SFX library, or the real-sfx skill with uisfx cues; earshot to check.

**Backed by:** [A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event), [SFX meanings: whoosh, pop, chime, thud](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-meaning-map), [Keyboard clicks and UI pops on bullets](../topics/sound.md#sound-ui-clicks-bullets), [AI sound stack: Real SFX + earshot](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-real-sfx-placement), [Horizontal wipes and slide-ins](../topics/transitions.md#tr-kinetic-wipes) · sources L01, L02, L06, L07, library

## Sparse accents on key beats
<a id="sparse-accents"></a>

About 10 SFX across 41 visual events; sound marks only what matters, plus a deliberate dropout.

**Looks like:** Most overlays enter silently. A pop on the price card, a hit on the real screenshot, a whoosh on the whip pan, and half a second of silence after the punchline.

**Good at:** emphasis means more; cleaner mix; faster to make

**Weak at:** the middle can feel flat; you need to choose the moments

**Best for:** formats reel60, reel90, yt-short · niches tech, all · goals retention, trust · effort low

**How:** Plan SFX in the storyboard's SCORE column; place 5–10 by hand.

**Backed by:** [Half-second music dropout after the punchline](../topics/sound.md#l10-dropout-after-punchline), [SCORE and EMPHASIS lines per beat](../topics/sound.md#l10-storyboard-score-emphasis), [A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event), [AI sound stack: Real SFX + earshot](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-real-sfx-placement), [Subtle 105–110% punch-in on key phrases](../topics/effects.md#fx-subtle-punch-in) · sources L10

## Cinematic impacts and risers
<a id="cinematic-impacts"></a>

Bass hits on key text, risers and sub-booms at chapter edges, metallic thuds, CRT static.

**Looks like:** A riser builds into '$100,000/MONTH', a sub-boom lands with the text, and a metallic thud ends the reel before black.

**Good at:** drama; teasers; chapter structure

**Weak at:** over the top for casual content; loud

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short, yt-long · niches gym, gaming, tech · goals reach, retention · effort medium

**How:** Risers, booms and hits from CC0 Openverse; placed with real-sfx; checked with earshot.

**Backed by:** [Bass hit on every key text pop](../topics/sound.md#sound-bass-hit-text-pop), [Chapter sounds: risers, booms, set foley](../topics/sound.md#sound-riser-sub-boom-chapters), [AI sound stack: Real SFX + earshot](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-real-sfx-placement), [A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event) · sources L08, L07

## Meme stingers
<a id="meme-stingers"></a>

Vine boom, record scratch, bass drop, scream stingers on reveals and punchlines.

**Looks like:** The weak-looking guy lifts the bar: record scratch, freeze, vine boom. Pure comedy timing.

**Good at:** comedy; shares; gaming and prank formats

**Weak at:** cheapens serious content; the library is missing for now

**Best for:** formats reel30, yt-short · niches gym, gaming · goals shares, reach · effort low

**How:** Edits/CapCut meme sound library; our own meme SFX library is not built yet.

**Backed by:** [Meme cutaways with the product pasted in](../topics/editing.md#edit-meme-cutaways), [SFX meanings: whoosh, pop, chime, thud](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-meaning-map), [Chapter sounds: risers, booms, set foley](../topics/sound.md#sound-riser-sub-boom-chapters), [B&W freeze for sarcastic punchlines](../topics/effects.md#fx-bw-freeze-punchline), [Sell a long video with a hyper-edited teaser](../topics/editing.md#edit-teaser-hyper-edited) · sources research

## No SFX, dialogue only
<a id="none"></a>

Voice (and maybe music) only.

**Looks like:** A conversation or vlog with no added sounds; the voice carries it.

**Good at:** authentic; podcasts; speed

**Weak at:** graphics feel weightless; 'silent movie' risk

**Best for:** formats podcast, yt-long, story · niches all · goals speed, trust · effort low

**How:** Nothing to add.

**Backed by:** [Podcast body: long takes, demos as interrupts](../topics/editing.md#edit-podcast-long-takes), [A sound on every visual event](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-every-event), [AI sound stack: Real SFX + earshot](../topics/ai-tools.md#ai-real-sfx-placement), [SFX meanings: whoosh, pop, chime, thud](../topics/sound.md#sound-sfx-meaning-map), [Quiet music bed near −22 to −24 dB](../topics/sound.md#sound-quiet-bed-throughout) · sources L08

## Mixing
L07 uses every-event UI sounds plus cinematic chapter impacts. L10 pairs sparse accents with a music dropout. The C13 clash is partly this choice: every event vs selective.

## Rule of thumb
Graphic-heavy teaching: every event. Clean premium reels: sparse accents. Teasers and hype: cinematic. Comedy: meme stingers. Podcasts: none.
